div.head: Af El. 2
div.ab: Ne minne noman ne cig ðu on idelnesse; forðon þe ðu ne bist unscyldig wið me, gif ðu on idelnesse cigst minne noman.
Ne minne naman ne cig ðu on idelnesse; forðon ðe þu ne byst unscyldig wið me, gif ðu on idelnesse cigst minne naman.
Ne minne naman ne cig þu on ydelnesse; forðam þu ne byst unscyldig wið me, gif þu on idelnesse (ge)cygst minne naman.
Non assumes nomen domini Dei tui in uanum. Nec enim habebit Dominus insontem eum qui assumpserit nomen domini Dei frustra.
Ne minne noman ne cig ðu on idelnesse; forðon þe ðu ne bist unscyldig wið me, gif ðu on idelnesse cigst minne noman.
Meinen Namen rufe du nicht zur Nichtigkeit an, weil du nicht ohne Schuld mir gegenüber bist, wenn du zur Nichtigkeit meinen Namen anrufst.
Do not call upon my name for vanity, because you are not without guilt towards me if you call upon my name for vanity.
You will not invoke my name idly: for you will not be guiltless with me, if you take my name idly.

note.seg: Vielleicht erklärt sich diese Abweichung aus non periurabis in nomine meo Levit. 19, 12. — Agsä. Zitate aus Ex. 20, 7—21, 17 in Ælfrics Homilien sammelt Cooke Bibl. quotations 90f.
Perhaps this departure is to be explained from non periurabis in nomine meo Levit. 19, 12. — A.-S. quotations from Ex. 20, 7—21, 17 in Ælfric’s homilies are collected by Cooke Bibl. quotations 90f.
‘sprich eitel, utter idly’ Frühere, dem Hebräischen gemäss; allein cigan heisst (in)vocare, clamare
‘speak vainly, utter idly’ earlier scholars, in accordance with the Hebrew; but cigan means (in)vocare, clamare
